responses.text: (1) README, Conditions, 'Covered in particular': the limit on n_rows is now attributed to in_off ((n_rows - 1)*input_row_stride < 2^31), not to the buffer lengths. (2) Err.lean, lane_facts: the docstring now states the bound the theorem proves, (2^-22 + 2^-33)*a + (3*2^-24 + 2^-33)*(w*a) + 2^-139 with w = mx - xs j = |s|, as exp_lane gives it. Wording only; no statement or proof changed, and the gate digest is the same.

README, Conditions, 'Covered in particular' now says that an input is covered while its last row starts below element 2^31. That is 131072 rows of 16384 columns (131072 x 16384, exactly 2^31 elements, is covered) and 169467 rows of 12672 columns (2^31 + 2176 elements). The limit is the last row's start, not the element count. Beyond it the int32 product row_idx * input_row_stride wraps, the kernel's own limit; the column offsets are added to the 64-bit pointer. Wording only; the gate digest is unchanged.
